record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: Can the existence of electromagnetic duality be tested experimentally through measured axion couplings?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, could it be tested experimentally through axion couplings whether there is an electromagnetic duality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In a theory containing an axion field $a$ coupled to electromagnetism through interactions of the form $\mathcal{L} \supset -	frac{1}{4} g_{a\gamma\gamma}\, a\, F_{\mu
u}	ilde F^{\mu
u}$ together with possible couplings to additional gauge sectors, the electromagnetic field strength $F_{\mu
u}$ and its Hodge dual $	ilde F^{\mu
u} = 	frac{1}{2}\varepsilon^{\mu
uho\sigma}F_{ho\sigma}$ enter symmetrically only under an electromagnetic duality transformation that rotates electric and magnetic degrees of freedom into one another (and, in the presence of magnetic charges, rotates electric and magnetic couplings, including any axion-induced contributions such as a Witten-effect-type shift of dyon charges). Consider experimentally accessible axion couplings, in particular the axion–photon coupling $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ together with axion couplings to leptons, quarks, nucleons, and any putative dark-sector gauge bosons, as functions of the underlying model parameters (e.g., Peccei–Quinn charges, anomaly coefficients, and mixing parameters between visible and hidden $U(1)$ sectors).
\
Question: Determine whether the presence or absence of an exact electromagnetic duality symmetry in the underlying theory imposes relations or constraints among these measurable axion couplings that are sharp enough to be distinguished, in principle, by a finite collection of laboratory and astrophysical measurements of axion couplings. Equivalently, exhibit an explicit set of coupling relations (or inequalities) that hold if and only if electromagnetic duality is an exact symmetry of the axion sector, or prove that no such experimentally distinguishing relations exist.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open conceptual question in axion physics. No experimental program or theoretical derivation is known that uses measured axion couplings as a sharp test of electromagnetic duality; current axion experiments (ADMX, haloscopes, helioscopes such as IAXO) aim only at detecting individual couplings, not at testing duality structure. The question therefore remains open.
